results.summary: This is a washing machine controller implemented as a finite state machine in Verilog. It simulates a simplified washing process with stages controlled by start, mode select, and door closed inputs. External hardware required includes LEDs, a debounced button, and two levers. The design is a straightforward educational example of a state machine for a household appliance.

This is an 8-bit SUBNEG CPU that requires external parallel SRAM for program and data storage. It interfaces with external address and output latches, and the program must be loaded into SRAM by an external microcontroller before enabling the CPU. The design outputs internal CPU state bits for debugging. It is a minimal, educational CPU implementation.

This is a basic oscilloscope and signal generator implemented on an ASIC. It samples an external ADC, buffers data on external FRAM, and displays the waveform via an HDMI Pmod. The signal generator produces sine, square, triangle, and sawtooth waveforms using direct digital synthesis. External hardware includes multiple Pmods for ADC, DAC, FRAM, HDMI, buttons, and switches.

This is a simple game that detects which of eight buttons was pressed first. When a button is pressed, its corresponding LED lights up and all other inputs are ignored. It requires eight buttons and eight LEDs as external hardware. The design is a straightforward demonstration of a priority latch.

This is an analog multiplexer module built with passgates, configurable as a 4:1 or 8:1 mux. It includes a ring oscillator and counter to drive the mux at high frequencies for characterization. External analog test equipment is needed to evaluate performance. The design is intended for debugging and inspecting analog signals in other projects.

This is a Brokaw bandgap voltage reference that produces a stable ~1.2V output and includes a PTAT temperature readout. It uses SKY130 PNP BJTs and an OTA-based summing amplifier. No external hardware is required beyond a 1.8V supply. The design is suitable for temperature sensing and voltage reference applications.

This is a simple I2C master controller that transmits one byte to a fixed slave address (0x50). It generates START and STOP conditions and provides BUSY, DONE, and ACK status outputs. External hardware required is an I2C slave device or a logic analyzer. The design is a minimal, educational I2C transmitter.

This is a high-speed crystal oscillator (HSXO) IP block wrapped for Tiny Tapeout. It requires an external passive crystal, load capacitors, and a 1uA bias current to generate a clock output. The design supports crystals between 4 and 16 MHz. It is a test chip for the oscillator IP.

This design reads up to six external photodiodes as digital inputs and displays the count on a 7-segment display. It can also be tested with dip switches instead of photodiodes. External hardware includes photodiodes, resistors, and a breadboard. The project is a simple educational light intensity sensor.

This is a 52-entry 6-bit FIFO implemented with a chain of latches for the first 48 entries and flip-flops for the last four. It supports write, pop, and peek operations with a ready signal to indicate write availability. External hardware is minimal, just a clock source and input switches. The design is an educational demonstration of a hybrid latch/flip-flop FIFO.
